why: Scheduling with durations and unlimited workers is the longest path in a DAG: a job starts at the latest finish among its prerequisites. Process jobs in topological order so every prerequisite's finish time is known first.
hints: When can job v start, at the earliest, if you know when each of its prerequisites finishes?
start[v] = max over prerequisites u of start[u] + durations[u]. Compute it in topological order so each u is final before v.
Kahn's algorithm with in-degrees; when popping u, push its finish time into start[v] = max(start[v], start[u] + durations[u]). Output start and start + duration per job. O(N + E).
pitfalls: The edge is [before, after]: before -> after.
Return pairs in job-index order, not in processing order.
